posts.title: The Theology of Clouds
posts.subhead: What remains from the faith my mother gave me
posts.excerpt: When I was very little, my nascent view of theology came from my mother. But it wasn't any instruction rooted in the Bible or any other religious text, or even from her anecdotal experience. No, she taught me to look up at the clouds to see God. That's where he lived. In retrospect, it's a beautiful perspective to impress upon a child. God and Jesus amongst the clouds, not separate from my world, just higher in the sky so they could look down and take care of me.

posts.title: Knowledge That Becomes Love
posts.excerpt: Core thought: Christlike knowledge begins in humility, sees people mercifully, and proves itself in love. I last had the opportunity to speak in church back in 2022, when I was on the cusp of my first wedding anniversary. It’s a testament to the rapid nature of life that four years have already passed us by, bringing with it the natural highs and lows of an ordinary mortal life. By virtue of the recent combination of wards, I wanted to briefly introduce my family to y’all.

posts.title: Still Out There
posts.subhead: I’m not sitting still long enough
posts.excerpt: It’s fine. It’s honestly just…fine. Say what you will about life. Think what you will about the passing of time, about the rotation of the Earth on its axis, of the orbital jurisdictions we undergo as human beings. Gravity has its hold on us, and we are not flung into space. That’s something grand to celebrate. It just boggles my mind to comprehend that I am 47 years old. Those precious memories I created as a teenager are becoming distant memories. My hips always hurt. My physical therapist is half my age.

posts.title: Level One
posts.subhead: What a 47 year old solo dev learns the hard way.
posts.excerpt: I’ve always wanted to make a video game, and I’m pretty envious of people who have the know how. Come to think of it, I’m envious of any kind of artistic know how. When I was really young, I remember being incredibly jealous of my oldest brother, Adam, who had a knack for sketching and drawing. One in particular burned itself into my memory: a picture of a helicopter hanging on his wall just above the doorway. I’m not sure if he knew, but I would sneak downstairs often to stare at all of his creations.

posts.title: A whole lot of nothing.
posts.subhead: What do you expect? I'm just one person.
posts.excerpt: Updated July 30, 2026 — The project has been delayed. I'll share a new launch date when I have one. I've been busy elsewhere this week, so I don't have a feature essay or even a rumination to share on this here blog. Instead, I can only share with you the promise that something relatively good is coming, and I am having fun preparing it. I think it is safe to say that it is not a book, not another large essay, and not even a Web site feature or update. Instead, it is a new app. That's all I will say for now.

posts.title: Balance is usually a myth
posts.excerpt: At church today, we were given about 15 minutes to consider a topic together amongst a group of men. Ages in the room ranged from late teens to young fathers in their mid 20s and early 30s, several of us in our late 40s and 50s, and a few older still. There were bountiful and sundry opinions and life experiences in that room. Fifteen minutes wasn't enough. The question, as best I remember it: How do we find time as providers to also be present with our family? I loved so many of the answers.

posts.title: The Midweek Weather
posts.excerpt: Greetings, everybody. I’ve been busy here, toiling away during my evenings. It’s good to have a hobby, neh? Or many hobbies, many hobbies that conflict with each other and cause me to lose focus and procrastinate the work I know is way more important. Yes. That too. Over the past few weeks, I just knew there was something wrong with my app. Have you ever noticed a problem with anything, and you know you have to take time to deal with it, but you simply don't have the confidence to do so?

posts.title: Can we take a break from cynicism?
posts.subhead: A lot of people had to put this back together just for you to roll your eyes at it.
posts.excerpt: Oh, my gosh. What should have been a remarkably fun announcement from Marvel and Disney has taken on a life of its own. And I am not surprised. But yeah...I'm still disappointed. For those who may not have heard yet, Marvel Studios released the first full trailer for Avengers: Doomsday on July 20. The movie arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026. The timing was interesting. San Diego Comic Con officially begins July 23, with Preview Night on July 22.

posts.title: Cruising Around Couches
posts.subhead: Rereading April 2009 from the other end of it.
posts.excerpt: Came across an old blog post last week. 17 years ago. I am intensely happy that I put forth the effort to record anything about those years. The snippet about the Hackintosh hit just right. Those were fine days, with narrow budgets and heady motivation to improvise. The machine in question was a Dell Inspiron Mini 9, and it was easily one of the most important devices in my DIY history. Every component of that machine was seemingly purpose built for the hack job.

posts.title: The Midweek Weather
posts.excerpt: Did you know that I love taking mushrooms? Settle that into your brainpan a little bit before I proceed. Ready? Without wading into far too much detail about the clinical side of life, I do have certain tendencies that make it harder for me to concentrate on a single task. And when I don't have a buffer, the world changes.

posts.title: What the Shade Is Called
posts.subhead: Vocabulary is more than language. It is personal scripture.
posts.excerpt: I. Noise Without Language This essay is about a painting. I framed the outline with that in mind. I had it nailed down. But at the end of it, I bet we will all agree the painting had nothing to do with it. But before we take that journey, before the painting ever hung in my teenage bedroom, there were thoughts without language. Instinct without purpose. The OCD mind. I want to properly set the stage and illustrate, as best I can, that my mind was already misfiring by the time I was five years old.

posts.title: The Midweek Weather
posts.subhead: This entry about a concert wasn't supposed to be about a concert at all
posts.excerpt: I am going to go back to my roots of organic, off the cuff writing once per week. While I am having the time of my life diving deep into the realms of religion, technology, and pop culture, I miss the times I would open up Blogger, dash off a (witty to me) explosion of thought, hit submit, and move on. Ideally, these entries will post sometime on Wednesdays, lending credibility to their name.

posts.title: Religion fills me with anger. God does not.
posts.subhead: P.S.: agency is not an excuse for lazy certainty.
posts.excerpt: About a week ago, Meta’s algorithm found it necessary to present me with a Facebook post. It arrived wearing the colors of religion. And while that made the whole thing more suspect, it was still useful. Silly algorithms are rarely pastoral, but occasionally, the stars align and they are timely. It was penned (typed? Bleated? Excreted?) by a man named Rexford, who described himself as having spent thirty eight years as a faithful Latter day Saint. He framed it as a labor of love. A warning. A careful explanation.

posts.title: Who Is Taking Care of the Thing That Took Care of Us?
posts.subhead: How the children of cartridges inherited a medium increasingly shaped by risk.
posts.excerpt: When I was 10 years old, just after school ended on a cold winter Friday, I walked into the local movie rental store off of 500 south in Bountiful, Utah. The building had an angled roofline and double doors, and when you stepped inside, the ceiling opened upward with exposed beams that made the place feel larger than it probably was. Huge, at least to me. The counter was near the front middle. To my left, there was a poster of Michael Keaton starring in his latest movie, Clean and Sober.

posts.title: Every Solution Has an Expiration Date
posts.subhead: On adulthood, technological fragility, and the exhaustion beneath adaptation.
posts.excerpt: I've had some less than casual observations lately about the world we find ourselves in. This began as a stream of thought essay, so prepare yourselves. Example: the surging prices of technological commodities such as RAM. Tim Cook explained it during a recent interview as a “100 year flood,” the likes of which he admitted he had not experienced in any area during his 40 years in the industry. It all feels so...exhausting.

posts.title: The Crucible of Continuous Revelation
posts.subhead: Navigating Same Sex Relationships Within the Restoration
posts.excerpt: A Note Before You Read This essay is the result of weeks of research, meditation, prayer, and revision. It is also the result of a much longer struggle: my attempt to understand the world more honestly, loosen my grip on comfortable assumptions, and listen beyond the rooms where I already feel agreed with. It is not an attempt to settle the argument for everyone.

posts.title: Different Mercies of the Same Light
posts.subhead: A night alone in the desert, the Milky Way, and a glimpse of heaven’s hidden unity
posts.excerpt: It is a rare occasion for me to be truly solitary. However, two Fridays back, an unexpected stillness settled in: my wife was away on her routine trip to California, and my children were either out of town or staying with their mother. I hadn’t anticipated this sudden isolation, and the realization hit me with a sense of urgency. The prospect of returning to an empty house and sitting in silence felt suddenly unbearable.

posts.title: Painted Worlds
posts.excerpt: I grew up alongside Nintendo. Not in the abstract way people say they “grew up with” something now, when what they mostly mean is that it was around. I mean Nintendo was part of the geography of my childhood.

posts.title: Just, well...updating.
posts.excerpt: If I've been quiet, it's for a good reason. If I've neglected this site, know that I've focused my energies elsewhere. The frgmnts app is nearing a state of readiness that I didn't think was possible in the short time of its existence. I was targeting summer '26 for the App Store review process; now I am thinking it may come to fruition closer to end of April/early May. I believe the app to be feature ready for the 1.0 release.

posts.title: Introducing frgmnts
posts.excerpt: Something has been bothering me for a long time. Not in a vague, ambient way in the specific way that eventually makes a person stop complaining and start building. The social apps I use the ones most of us use were not designed to help me stay close to my people. They were designed to keep me producing, reacting, performing, and returning. The closeness is real enough to feel. The machinery underneath it is something else entirely. I wanted something smaller. Warmer. Less extractive.

posts.title: Not in my Nature
posts.excerpt: I hate keeping secrets. I don't hate the actual secrets themselves, but I have a hard time tamping them down. There is, after all, an art to timing, and value to be found in well aged and mature processes. And I do love the moment of unveiling! Especially if the secret maintained itself well and was a pleasant surprise unto all it was revealed. Walking into a weekend shortly, and we are starting it off by a trip to the movies to see the next Super Mario Bros movie. I don't care if it's good or not.

posts.title: Just checking in, y'all
posts.excerpt: The sheer volume of projects I have going right now is keeping me from attending to the most sincere and critical areas of OTW right now, but I promise it'll be worth it. Stay close to this feed for more information in the near future. The t shirt contest ended with a fair amount of success. It accomplished what I need it to: show people that OTW exists and deserves a place in their hearts. I am so appreciative of everyone who submitted entries, visited the site, and gave me feedback.

posts.title: 50 Best Apple Products
posts.excerpt: A wonderful bit of nostalgia bait posted to The Verge today. And they did it in the best way possible: a pitch perfect recreation of the Classic Mac OS. I wish I had more experience with the products the staff chose; items like the black MacBook, PowerBooks, and Bondi Blue iMac took me right back to working at Best Buy in the 1990s. Go ahead and check it out here. Don't be surprised if you get paralyzed between choices like I did with this one.

posts.title: A Map of the Sleeping Mind
posts.excerpt: Like most dreams, it just begins; dropped into the frame like an afterthought. What I see is familiar: cracked asphalt laid down decades ago, its surface buckled by gnarled tree roots and years of forgotten traffic. Faded yellow traffic lines trace the ground, bearing no further responsibility for direction. The mall facade is a stained archetype under the artificial lights.

posts.title: Back in the Saddle, pt 2
posts.excerpt: I think it's beyond time to swing this blog a little toward the positive side. So, what to talk about? Why, one of my favorite little hobbies since my youth: cycling. Back in July of '22, I posted a quiet note to Instagram that I was, indeed, "back in the saddle." The picture I posted was of my new bike, on which I rode from my home in Queen Creek all the way to the Mesa Temple. Geez, how many miles is that? Quick maths. Twenty four miles away from here. Which makes for a 48 mile round trip. That cannot be right.

posts.title: Resistance: The Primary
posts.excerpt: Tags: family Preface What spills forth below is the end result of the 649 days in between this very moment and the day my mom crossed the bridge to her next journey. It is the compendium of waking up relentlessly exhausted, dreaming about her, night after night. These words attempt to encapsulate the endlessly conflictive journey that she and I took together, especially over the last 35 years.

posts.title: Just a midnight's summary
posts.excerpt: I've been busy here at OTW lately. Some things you may have noticed: 1. A brand new page, strictly for short form thoughts. I call it fragments. It's clearly inspired by Twitter/X. 2. A reformatted index/main page. I loved the star field, but it was too poetic and didn't point people in the right direction. So, it got the axe. 3. The t shirt giveaway has been extended. I admit I made it way too cumbersome to enter. So I relaxed the form and gave everyone an extra week.

posts.title: Wow...that came out of nowhere.
posts.excerpt: Hello, and welcome to Friday, weary travelers. My flickering hope for this week remains that at least some of you have stopped by from my social media posts. Of course, there's also my t shirt giveaway, and I would that everyone has a chance to find the secret and submit an entry. These shirts are the prettiest purple I could find, and you'll be one of only three humans to have it if you win the random drawing. In other news: My vacation ended at 5 p.m. today.

posts.title: Life is grand, getting grander
posts.excerpt: What a fabulous week off. Emily and I went the staycation route and nailed down a 2 night stay at the Hilton Phoenix Tapatio Cliffs Resort, which is near an area I used to frequent as a teenager. Driving through those hills gave me so many flashbacks. Even moving around the resort reminded me that decades ago, my aunt and uncle would bring their family to the valley and stay at Tapatio Cliffs.

posts.title: 47, or something...
posts.excerpt: I went into the day with such grand ambition. The first, a 23.5 mile bike ride, likely sabotaged the morning vibe. The bed was so soft, the house so enveloped in quiet, that to disentangle myself from the sheets was tantamount to blasphemy. Nevertheless, knowing a day of gluttony lay before me, the extra caloric buffer this ride would provide got me out of bed and on the road by 9 a.m. (Traveler's note: I did not ride 23.5 miles. 20.20 was all I had gas for.) Emily and Sadie joined me for 11:30 a.m.

posts.title: The MacBook Neo Makes an Awful Lot of Sense
posts.excerpt: Tags: Apple News, Tech News Once Upon a Time, my only recourse for helping friends and family get themselves into a Mac was to push them toward a Mac mini, but I always had reservations heading down that street. I knew it came with trade offs. What monitor would they use? Do they really enjoy their $9.99 keyboard/mouse combo? But the sweet, sweet price! It vacillated over the past decade, as low as $499 for the entry level model. It made the most sense.

posts.title: The Long Nap is Over
posts.excerpt: Maybe you're reading this because you're following a link from Facebook or Instagram. If so, congratulations! You made it out. It's just you and me now, my friend. I've had this site for 26 years. When I started outsidetheworld.com back in 2000, there were no Clouds or AIs, no iPhones, no music streaming services. I mean, most of us got our MP3s from Napster over AOL. I’ll be the first to admit that since about 2013, this place has been gathering some serious digital dust.

posts.title: So much...March
posts.excerpt: Already the 4th of March, which means it's already the 3rd month of this, the year of our Lord 2026... I may have learned most of what I needed to know in kindergarten, but no one prepared me for midlife. I never expected the burning demand on all sectors of my life to be turned up to such an intensity. I close my eyes and can catch glimpses of parallel universes flitting by, their courses set in motion by a million different daily decisions.

posts.title: Sunset Sublimity x2
posts.excerpt: The last two days have been a right treat for sunsets here in AZ. Tonight's in particular was especially tasty; one of those viciously red blasts that eminate on the horizon and paint the entire celestial dome with a thousand different shades of orange, pink, purple, and blue. Take a look: I was especially stoked for this display tonight, as my MIL was in town from Utah and can't get enough of the Sonoran skyscapes. She landed just in time to catch the tail end of it.

posts.title: A Brand New OTW, baby
posts.excerpt: Where have I heard that before? Surely, at least five times on this site during the past 26 years. 26 years, btw. That's how long I've had this domain registered and operating in one form or another. I finally felt the drive to really sit down and get all of the accumulated digital cruft organized and back online. So, what you see is the first stage of the process. I still haven't quite decided whether I will keep the site divided into Personal/Professional ongoing.

posts.title: Maybe, a poem?
posts.excerpt: For as far as you wish For as long as you stretch In the moment you lumber In haste, toward the mountain The general truth The uncourteous example Never minding the canopy Stretching, aching with heaviness Reminder, your cohort Believes in the coddling fervor The mind numbing ache The key turn freeing What's the angle, then? To a friend, just perspiration To our valley below, it's normality Do you remember the promise?

posts.title: It's a straight VIBE
posts.excerpt: Hallelujah, folks. We are back online and fully ready to rock this site back into existence. For the longest time, I fell back on 3rd party tools and services to help post thoughts to the ether. This was my mechanism for years after I fell into silence while my life took the crazy train without me (with me?) as a passenger. But I digress. Back in 2000, my original site was near pure HTML, with each page created lovingly within Microsoft FrontPage (remember that?)
